summary: Recorded won revenue is $10,005,534 across 4,238 won deals and 6,711 closed deals, with an overall win rate of 63.150%. Average sales are $2,360.91 and average weeks to close is 7.397. Open pipeline contains 2,089 opportunities; potential to close is $3,360,822 as estimated open-pipeline list price, with 333 unpriced open opportunities. Team win rates range from 62.084% to 64.430% by manager, with Summer Sewald and Cara Losch above the overall win rate and Rocco Neubert, Melvin Marxen, and Dustin Brinkmann below. Darcel Schlecht leads agent won revenue at $1,153,214. Quarterly close results show Q1 2017 win rate at 82.071% on 647 closed deals, then approximately 60%–62% in Q2–Q4; Q4 new opportunities fell 57.942% QoQ. Product conversion is strongest for MG Special (64.841%) and GTX Plus Pro (64.295%), while MG Advanced is lowest among the larger products at 60.332%; GTK 500 is 60.000% on a small sample. GTXPro is the top product by won revenue at $3,510,578. The open-pipeline figure is an estimated list-price potential and is not a probability-weighted forecast.

findings.question: How is each sales team performing compared to the rest?
findings.answer: By manager: Summer Sewald 64.336% win rate (+1.186 pp vs overall), Cara Losch 64.430% (+1.279 pp), Celia Rouche 63.410% (+0.260 pp), Dustin Brinkmann 62.985% (-0.165 pp), Melvin Marxen 62.200% (-0.950 pp), and Rocco Neubert 62.084% (-1.066 pp). Won revenue by manager: Melvin Marxen $2,251,930; Summer Sewald $1,964,750; Rocco Neubert $1,960,545; Celia Rouche $1,603,897; Cara Losch $1,130,049; Dustin Brinkmann $1,094,363. By region, win rates are West 63.940%, East 63.025%, and Central 62.558%.

findings.question: Are any sales agents lagging behind?
findings.answer: Darcel Schlecht leads agent won revenue at $1,153,214 (349 won deals, 63.110% win rate). Next are Vicki Laflamme $478,396, Kary Hendrixson $454,298, Cassey Cress $450,489, and Donn Cantrell $445,860. Highest agent win rates include Hayden Neloms 70.395% (107 won/152 closed), Maureen Marcano 69.953% (149/213), and Wilburn Farren 69.620% (55/79). Lowest agent win rates include Lajuana Vencill 54.978% (127/231), Markita Hansen 57.269% (130/227), Donn Cantrell 57.455% (158/275), and Gladys Colclough 58.190% (135/232). Agent opportunity counts vary from 110 to 747, so smaller samples should be interpreted cautiously.

findings.question: Are there any quarter-over-quarter trends?
findings.answer: 2017 close-quarter won revenue: Q1 $1,134,672 with 82.071% win rate (531 won/647 closed); Q2 $3,086,111 with 61.713% win rate (1,254 won/2,032 closed), +171.983% QoQ revenue; Q3 $2,982,255 with 61.407% win rate (1,257 won/2,047 closed), -3.365% QoQ revenue; Q4 $2,802,496 with 60.252% win rate (1,196 won/1,985 closed), -6.028% QoQ revenue. New opportunities by engage quarter: 2016-Q4 358; 2017-Q1 1,619 (+352.235% QoQ); 2017-Q2 2,388 (+47.498% QoQ); 2017-Q3 2,770 (+15.997% QoQ); 2017-Q4 1,165 (-57.942% QoQ).

findings.question: Do any products have better win rates?
findings.answer: Product win rates: MG Special 64.841% (793 won/1,223 closed; 1,651 opportunities); GTX Plus Pro 64.295% (479/745; 968 opportunities); GTX Basic 63.719% (915/1,436; 1,866 opportunities); GTXPro 63.557% (729/1,147; 1,480 opportunities); GTX Plus Basic 62.131% (653/1,051; 1,383 opportunities); MG Advanced 60.332% (654/1,084; 1,412 opportunities); GTK 500 60.000% (15/25; 40 opportunities; small sample).

recommendations.text: Focus coaching and pipeline review on agents with below-overall win rates and meaningful closed volume, such as Lajuana Vencill, Markita Hansen, Donn Cantrell, and Gladys Colclough, while accounting for sample-size differences.

Investigate product conversion differences: MG Special and GTX Plus Pro have the highest product win rates, while MG Advanced is lowest among the larger products; review qualification and sales enablement for lower-converting products.
Treat GTK 500 conclusions cautiously because it has only 40 opportunities and 25 closed deals in the supplied data.
Monitor the quarterly pattern: Q1 2017 had an 82.071% win rate on 647 closed deals, while Q2–Q4 win rates were approximately 60%–62%, and 2017-Q4 new opportunities fell 57.942% QoQ by engage quarter.

Use the $3,360,822 open-pipeline potential only as an estimated list-price figure, not as a probability-weighted forecast, and resolve the 333 unpriced open opportunities before drawing pipeline conclusions.
Prioritize top accounts Kan-code, Konex, Condax, Cheers, and Hottechi for retention and expansion, given their recorded won revenue.
Build sector playbooks around retail for largest won revenue and marketing for highest listed win rate, while reviewing finance where the listed win rate is lowest.
Address data-quality gaps, especially the 500 invalid engage dates, to improve confidence in engagement-quarter and opportunity-source reporting.
